title: AI Engineering
description: A practical path from machine-learning foundations to production retrieval-augmented generation, written for experienced software developers who are new to ML. You will learn how models learn from a loss, how neural networks are trained with backpropagation, how attention and Transformers work, and how to build and evaluate grounded RAG systems with hybrid search and citations.

concepts.name: Loss functions
concepts.description: How a single number measures how wrong a model is: MSE and MAE for regression, cross-entropy for classification, and the difference between a loss, a metric and an objective.

concepts.name: Gradient descent
concepts.description: Minimising a loss by repeatedly stepping against the gradient; learning rates, mini-batches, epochs, momentum and Adam.

concepts.name: Overfitting and regularization
concepts.description: Detecting overfitting with validation data and reducing it with L2/L1 penalties, weight decay, dropout, early stopping and more data.

concepts.name: Activation functions
concepts.description: Why neurons need non-linearities; sigmoid, tanh, ReLU, GELU and softmax, saturation, vanishing gradients and dead ReLUs.

concepts.name: Backpropagation
concepts.description: Computing every parameter's gradient efficiently with the chain rule: a forward pass that caches values, then a backward pass in which each layer multiplies the incoming gradient by its local derivative.

concepts.name: Embeddings
concepts.description: Dense learned vectors for tokens and passages, embedding tables, and similarity measures: dot product, cosine similarity and Euclidean distance.

concepts.name: Attention
concepts.description: Weighted averaging of values by query-key similarity, queries/keys/values projections, masking, and scaled dot-product attention with division by the square root of d_k.

concepts.name: Transformers
concepts.description: Multi-head attention, positional information (sinusoidal, learned, RoPE), and the Transformer block with residual connections, layer normalisation and feed-forward layers.

concepts.name: Chunking
concepts.description: Splitting documents into retrievable passages: size trade-offs, overlap, structure-aware splitting and chunk metadata for citations and filtering.

concepts.name: Vector search
concepts.description: Finding nearest-neighbour embeddings at scale: exact search costs, approximate indexes such as HNSW and IVF, recall, pgvector and filtering.

concepts.name: Hybrid search and RRF
concepts.description: Combining keyword search (BM25) with vector search and fusing their rankings with reciprocal rank fusion (k = 60), plus optional reranking.

concepts.name: RAG evaluation
concepts.description: Measuring retrieval (Recall@k, MRR, nDCG) and generation quality (groundedness, citation validity, refusals), golden datasets, calibrated LLM judges and confidence intervals.

modules.title: Foundations of machine learning
modules.summary: What it means for a model to learn: measuring error with a loss, minimising it with gradient descent, and making sure the result generalises beyond the training data.

lessons.title: What a model learns: loss functions
lessons.summary: Models learn whatever makes their loss small. Meet MSE, MAE and cross-entropy, and learn how a loss differs from a metric.
objectives: Explain the role of a loss function in training
Compute MSE, MAE and cross-entropy by hand
Choose an appropriate loss for regression and classification
Distinguish a loss from an evaluation metric

lessons.title: Gradient descent
lessons.summary: Follow the slope downhill: the update rule, why the learning rate matters, mini-batches, momentum and Adam.
objectives: State and apply the gradient descent update rule
Predict the effect of a learning rate that is too small or too large
Explain batch, stochastic and mini-batch gradient descent
Describe what momentum and Adam add to plain gradient descent

lessons.title: Overfitting and regularization
lessons.summary: Spot overfitting with validation data, then reduce it with weight decay, L1, dropout, early stopping and more data.
objectives: Diagnose overfitting and underfitting from training and validation curves
Compute L2 and L1 penalties and their effect on weights
Explain dropout and early stopping
Avoid data leakage between splits

modules.title: Neural networks
modules.summary: From a single neuron to a trained network: non-linear activations, backpropagation with the chain rule, and the practical engineering of a training run.

lessons.title: Neurons and activation functions
lessons.summary: A neuron is a weighted sum plus a non-linearity. Learn why the non-linearity matters and how sigmoid, tanh, ReLU and GELU compare.
objectives: Compute a neuron's output for a given activation
Explain why stacked linear layers collapse without activations
Explain saturation and vanishing gradients
Pick a suitable activation for hidden and output layers

lessons.title: Backpropagation and the chain rule
lessons.summary: Compute every gradient in one backward pass: each layer multiplies the incoming gradient by its local derivative, moving from the output backward.
objectives: Apply the chain rule through a computation graph
Run a forward and backward pass by hand on a small network
Explain why backpropagation is efficient
Connect products of local derivatives to vanishing and exploding gradients

lessons.title: Training neural networks in practice
lessons.summary: The training loop, initialisation, learning-rate schedules, Adam, normalisation, gradient clipping and a checklist for debugging runs.
objectives: Write and explain a standard training loop
Compute steps per epoch and plan a training budget
Explain warmup, Adam's first step and gradient clipping
Debug a training run systematically

modules.title: Attention mechanisms
modules.summary: How models represent tokens as vectors and let them exchange information: embeddings, attention, queries/keys/values, scaling, multiple heads, positions and the full Transformer block.

lessons.title: Embeddings and similarity
lessons.summary: Dense vectors that place related items close together, and the dot product, cosine and Euclidean measures used to compare them.
objectives: Explain why embeddings beat one-hot encodings
Compute dot product, cosine similarity and Euclidean distance
Explain how sentence embeddings enable semantic search
Apply practical rules for using embedding models

lessons.title: Attention basics
lessons.summary: Attention as a soft dictionary lookup: score, softmax, weighted sum — and why the scores must be scaled.
objectives: Describe attention as a weighted average of values
Compute attention weights and outputs for a small example
Explain why unscaled dot-product scores saturate the softmax
Define self-attention

lessons.title: Queries, keys and values
lessons.summary: Three learned projections give each token a query, a key and a value; masks control which tokens can see each other.
objectives: Explain the roles of queries, keys and values
Compute Q, K, V and attention outputs for two tokens
Apply causal and padding masks correctly
Distinguish self-attention from cross-attention

lessons.title: Scaled dot-product attention
lessons.summary: The full formula softmax(QK^T / sqrt(d_k)) V, why dot products grow with dimension, and how scaling prevents softmax saturation and vanishing gradients.
objectives: Write the scaled dot-product attention formula and explain each part
Derive that the variance of a dot product of d unit-variance entries is d
Explain why dividing by sqrt(d_k) keeps gradients healthy
Estimate the quadratic cost of attention

lessons.title: Multi-head attention
lessons.summary: Several attention heads in parallel, each in its own subspace, combined by an output projection; plus KV cache sizing and grouped-query attention.
objectives: Explain why multiple heads help
Compute head dimensions and parameter counts
Describe concatenation and the output projection
Estimate KV cache size and the effect of GQA

lessons.title: Positional information
lessons.summary: Attention ignores order unless we add it: sinusoidal and learned position embeddings, rotary embeddings (RoPE) and ALiBi.
objectives: Explain why self-attention is permutation-equivariant
Compute sinusoidal position encodings
Explain how RoPE makes scores depend on relative position
Describe the context-length limits of positional schemes

lessons.title: The Transformer block
lessons.summary: Attention plus a feed-forward network, wrapped in residual connections and layer normalisation, stacked into a language model.
objectives: Describe the pre-norm Transformer block
Explain how residual connections help training
Compute layer normalisation and parameter counts
Distinguish encoder-only, decoder-only and encoder-decoder models

modules.title: Retrieval-augmented generation
modules.summary: Grounding model answers in your own documents: chunking, vector and hybrid search with reciprocal rank fusion, and evaluating retrieval and citations.

lessons.title: Why RAG: grounding answers
lessons.summary: Why models need retrieval, how a RAG pipeline works, grounding and citations, context budgets, and RAG versus fine-tuning.
objectives: Explain the limits of a model's built-in knowledge
Describe the indexing and answering halves of RAG
Plan a context-window budget for retrieved passages
Explain why retrieved text must be treated as data

lessons.title: Chunking documents
lessons.summary: Split documents into passages that embed precisely and carry complete thoughts: sizes, overlap, structure-aware splitting and metadata.
objectives: Explain the chunk-size trade-off
Count chunks for a given size and overlap
Choose a chunking strategy for different document types
Store metadata that supports citations and filtering

lessons.title: Vector search and HNSW
lessons.summary: From brute-force kNN to approximate indexes: how HNSW navigates a layered graph, its tuning knobs, IVF, pgvector and filtering.
objectives: Estimate the memory and compute cost of exact search
Explain how HNSW search works
Tune M, ef_construction and ef_search for recall and latency
Use pgvector operators and indexes correctly

lessons.title: Hybrid search and reciprocal rank fusion
lessons.summary: Combine BM25 keyword search with vector search, fuse rankings with RRF (k = 60), and optionally rerank.
objectives: Explain when keyword search beats vector search and vice versa
Describe the main ideas of BM25
Compute reciprocal rank fusion scores with k = 60
Design a hybrid retrieval pipeline

lessons.title: Evaluating retrieval and citations
lessons.summary: Golden datasets, Recall@k, MRR and nDCG, groundedness and citation checks, calibrated LLM judges and confidence intervals.
objectives: Build a golden dataset for retrieval and answers
Compute Recall@k, MRR and nDCG
Validate citations and groundedness
Interpret evaluation results with confidence intervals
